claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9293 s2.2: "TCP provides a reliable, in-order, byte-stream service to applications." ... "TCP reliability consists of detecting packet losses (via sequence numbers) ... as well as correction via retransmission." Scoped by "while that connection lasts".

RFC 9293: state is kept in a TCB holding "the local and remote IP addresses and port numbers". s3.6: "A TCP connection may terminate in two ways: (1) the normal TCP close sequence using a FIN handshake ... and (2) an 'abort'" - "normally" covers this. RFC 791 s1.4: IP has "no acknowledgments either end-to-end or hop-by-hop".
claim_verdicts.source: rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.txt s3.3.1 l.626-635, s3.6 l.1627; rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791.txt s1.4

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9293 Figure 6 "Basic Three-Way Handshake": line 2 <CTL=SYN>, line 3 <CTL=SYN,ACK>, line 4 <CTL=ACK>.

RFC 791: "The internet protocol does not provide a reliable communication facility ... There are no retransmissions." RFC 768: "delivery and duplicate protection are not guaranteed". RFC 1035 s4.2.1: "Queries or their responses may be reordered by the network".

RFC 768: "The protocol is transaction oriented, and delivery and duplicate protection are not guaranteed. Applications requiring ordered reliable delivery of streams of data should use the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)." Header has only ports, length, checksum.

RFC 9293 after Figure 6: "At line 4, TCP Peer A responds with an empty segment containing an ACK for TCP Peer B's SYN; and in line 5, TCP Peer A sends some data." Line 4 is not answered; data leaves after one round trip (SYN out, SYN-ACK back).
RFC 9293: "A connection is defined by a pair of sockets." TCB variables include "the local and remote IP addresses and port numbers".

Now conditioned on "from the same machine". RFC 9293 s3.4.1: "A connection is defined by a pair of sockets." RFC 9112 s9: "Most servers are designed to maintain thousands of concurrent connections". Lab: two concurrent `nc localhost 8080` -> ss shows ESTABLISHED ::1:44264<->::1:8080 and ::1:44266<->::1:8080 at the same time.
claim_verdicts.source: rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.txt s3.4.1; refs/rfc/rfc9112.txt l.1302-1303; examples/don-hang@stage-0 (ff911b0), run in donhang-lab 2026-09-27 (round 3)

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9293 s2.2: "detecting packet losses (via sequence numbers) ... as well as correction via retransmission"; s3.3.1: "A segment on the retransmission queue is fully acknowledged if..." - receiver acknowledges, sender keeps and resends.

RFC 768 header: Source Port, Destination Port, Length, Checksum - no sequence number, no ack/retransmission defined. "UDP itself" correctly leaves room for RFC 791: "Errors detected may be reported via the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP)".

Re-run of stage-0 script in lab, timestamped per line: nc prints "Connection to localhost (::1) 8080 port [tcp/http-alt] succeeded!" only for check 1 and the two runs of the last check; checks 2 and 3 show only the script echo "(exit code 1)". Checks 1-3 end connected / refused at 32 ms / gave up at ~3.0 s. `nc -h`: "OpenBSD netcat (Debian patchlevel 1.234-1)", "-z Zero-I/O mode".

compose@stage-0: web image caddy:2.10.0, network_mode "service:lab"; Caddyfile site ":8080". Run prints the quoted line verbatim. Lab `grep -w 8080 /etc/services` -> "http-alt 8080/tcp webcache # WWW caching service".
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang@stage-0 (ff911b0), run in donhang-lab 2026-09-27 (round 3); docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9293 s3.5.2: "If the connection does not exist (CLOSED), then a reset is sent in response to any incoming segment except another reset. A SYN segment that does not match an existing connection is rejected by this means." Lab: check 2 line printed ~5 ms after its heading, exit code 1.
claim_verdicts.source: rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.txt s3.5.2; examples/don-hang@stage-0 (ff911b0), run in donhang-lab 2026-09-27 (round 3)

claim_verdicts.evidence: `nc -h`: "-w timeout  Timeout for connects and final net reads". Timed run: check 3 line printed at 3025 ms vs heading at 39 ms, exit code 1. Without -w: `timeout 8 nc -z 203.0.113.1 80` -> rc=124 after 8 s, so it waits longer than 3 s.
RFC 5737: "The blocks 192.0.2.0/24 (TEST-NET-1), 198.51.100.0/24 (TEST-NET-2), and 203.0.113.0/24 (TEST-NET-3) are provided for use in documentation."

Execution: script output shows `$?` after `||` printing nc's exit code 1 for checks 2 and 3; `&&` in check 1 and the last check prints only after success. Matches bash list semantics (round 2 lab checks `false || echo "a $?"` -> "a 1", `false && echo c` -> nothing).

RFC 4291 s2.5.3: "The unicast address 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 is called the loopback address. It may be used by a node to send an IPv6 packet to itself." "An IPv6 packet with a destination address of loopback must never be sent outside of a single node".

RFC 9112 s9: "the \"http\" URI scheme (Section 4.2.1 of [HTTP]) indicates a default connection of TCP over IP, with a default TCP port of 80". Lesson conditions it with "as you meet it here"; Caddy serves the lab over plain TCP on :8080.
RFC 8446 s1: "the only requirement from the underlying transport is a reliable, in-order data stream." TLS runs on top of the opened TCP connection.

RFC 9293 s3.5.2: a SYN with no matching connection "is rejected by this means" (reset). k8s docs: "A connection refused error is expected because the API server is not yet running. A timeout, however, means the load balancer cannot communicate with the control plane node." Lesson says "may be wrong".
RFC 1035: UDP "is the recommended method for standard queries in the Internet. Queries sent using UDP may be lost, and hence a retransmission strategy is required."

Conditional opinion ("worth it when ... and the asker can simply ask again"), consistent with RFC 768 ("minimum of protocol mechanism") and RFC 1035 recommending UDP with retransmission for standard queries.
RFC 9293 s3.6.1: "Since the two directions of a TCP connection are closed independently, it is possible for a connection to be 'half closed', i.e., closed in only one direction".

RFC 6056 s1: "The IP address and port number of the client are normally left unspecified by the client application and thus are chosen automatically by the client networking stack." Lab: ip_local_port_range 32768 60999; observed client ports 44264, 44266 (51000 in the diagram is inside that range).
claim_verdicts.source: rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6056.txt s1; examples/don-hang@stage-0 (ff911b0), run in donhang-lab 2026-09-27 (round 3)

claim_verdicts.evidence: tcp-connect.sh@stage-0 l.5 (2nd line of the quoted block, lines=4-20): `[ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec "$(dirname "$0")/../lab-run.sh" "$0" "$@"`; lab-run.sh ends `exec docker compose exec -T lab bash -c ...` ("so that its output is the same on Windows, macOS, Linux and CI"). compose: lab publishes "8080:8080", web uses network_mode "service:lab".

issues.quote: a timeout is no answer at all, usually a wrong address or something dropping packets
issues.text: "usually" is a frequency claim with no evidence and not in the ledger; section 6 and claim 21 say only "may". The summary is stronger than the body.
issues.fix: Write "a timeout is no answer at all: the address may be wrong or something in between may be dropping packets."

issues.quote: The heading says "at the same time", but these two runs happen one after the other
issues.text: Repo-side, unchanged at stage-0: tcp-connect.sh l.19 heading promises simultaneous connections, l.20 chains the two nc runs with `&&`. The lesson now states this honestly; the workaround sentence exists only because of the script. Already in meta repo_changes_needed.
issues.fix: Owner: accept the repo_changes_needed entry (echo "one server port, one connection after another:", recapture output), then drop the sentence "The heading says ... one after the other" and keep "the listener takes a second connection as readily as the first".

issues.quote: TCP — a way of moving bytes between two ports
issues.text: Claims 1-10, 14, 16, 18, 20-24, 26 rest on RFC 9293/768/791/5737/4291/1035/6056/8446 fetched from rfc-editor.org; only rfc9110/9457/6749/7519/8446 are docs roots in content/versions.yaml, no version_key is set, and nc (OpenBSD netcat, Debian 1.234-1 in the lab) is not pinned. Unchanged from round 2.
issues.fix: Owner: add a `standards: tcp_ip` entry (RFC 9293, 768, 791) to content/versions.yaml, optionally mirror into refs/rfc/, then set version_key on those claims. No lesson text change.

issues.quote: A tab's `localhost:8080` on your own machine is passed on to the same Caddy.
issues.text: The prereq taught me localhost names the machine running the command, so my tab's localhost is my laptop, not the lab box. 'Passed on' tells me that it reaches Caddy but not what does the passing, so I accept it without understanding why my laptop's port 8080 leads into the lab box.
issues.fix: Add a few words naming who passes it on, e.g. 'the lab is set up so that port 8080 on your own machine is handed on to the same Caddy'.

issues.quote: Every command ends with a number, 0 when it worked and something else when it did not, and `$?` prints that number.
issues.text: The sentence before says 'only its exit code says so', and this sentence explains the number, but never says that this number is the exit code. I linked them only from '(exit code $?)' in the script.
issues.fix: Write 'Every command ends with a number, its exit code: 0 when it worked ...'.

issues.quote: Your data waits only for message 2, the box's answer. Message 3 needs no answer of its own, so your data follows it straight away: the wait is one trip out and back.
issues.text: I had to read this twice to see why three messages cost only one trip: the step 'message 1 goes out, message 2 comes back, that is the trip' is left for me to assemble.
issues.fix: Add before 'the wait': 'message 1 going out and message 2 coming back is that trip'.

issues.quote: The heading says "at the same time", but these two runs happen one after the other
issues.text: The script prints a heading that the prose then tells me not to believe. I follow the correction, but it leaves me unsure what the last check proves about 'several connections at once'; for that I rely on the tab example, not the script.
issues.fix: Keep the sentence until the script heading is changed; then drop it, as the rest of the paragraph already says what the check shows.

issues.quote: Name lookups work this way: the question goes out over UDP
issues.text: I know DNS turns names into addresses, and I guess 'name lookups' means DNS, but the lesson never says so in this section; only the Connections line hints at it.
